evidence.observation: The core subprocess runner. It launches subprocess.Popen with stdout=subprocess.PIPE and stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, so stderr is merged into the stdout pipe; text=True/universal_newlines plus encoding and errors="replace" decode the bytes. It then captures output incrementally by reading process.stdout one character at a time (read(1)), printing each chunk to the console in real time and appending it to an in-memory list. After the stream ends it calls process.wait() and returns the tuple (process.returncode, "".join(output)). Critically, no timeout argument (and no timer/poll mechanism) is passed to Popen, so a hung command blocks forever. Any exception is swallowed and reported as return code 1 with the exception string as output.

Public entry point and dispatch layer. If stdin is a TTY and pexpect is available and the platform is not Windows, it delegates to run_cmd_pexpect for interactive pass-through; otherwise it delegates to run_cmd_subprocess. It catches OSError only, returning the tuple (1, error_message) and routing the message either to print or to the supplied error_print callable. It forwards cwd but introduces no timeout of its own.

The interactive branch. It resolves $SHELL (falling back to /bin/sh) and spawns it as pexpect.spawn(shell, args=["-i", "-c", command], encoding="utf-8", cwd=cwd), falling back to spawning the command directly when the shell path does not exist. child.interact(output_filter=output_callback) gives control to the user while the filter copies all bytes into a BytesIO buffer. It then calls child.close() and returns (child.exitstatus, output.getvalue().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")). No timeout is configured, so interact runs until the child exits (child.exitstatus can be None when the child is killed by a signal). pexpect.ExceptionPexpect/TypeError/ValueError are caught and converted to (1, error_msg).

The linter's command runner and exit-status consumer. It appends the shell-quoted filename (oslex.quote(rel_fname)) to the command and calls run_cmd_subprocess(cmd, cwd=self.root, encoding=self.encoding), capturing only the returned stdout into `errors`. Exit-status handling is explicit: returncode == 0 is treated as 'no lint problems' and the method returns None; a non-zero return code builds a block prefixed with '## Running: {cmd}' plus the captured errors and hands it to errors_to_lint_result (which parses file:line references and builds a LintResult). OSError from executing the command is caught, printed, and also returns None. No timeout is applied.

A separate capture path that does not use run_cmd_subprocess. It invokes subprocess.run([...flake8...], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, encoding=self.encoding, errors="replace", cwd=self.root) and manually merges streams with errors = result.stdout + result.stderr. check=False means the exit status is never consulted; a lint result is produced only when the concatenated output is non-empty. A broad 'except Exception' turns a launch failure into the synthetic text 'Error running flake8: ...'. Like the other paths, no timeout is passed to subprocess.run.

The only test for run_cmd. It executes the real command 'echo Hello, World!' and asserts the returned exit code is 0 and that the captured output strips to exactly 'Hello, World!', covering exit-status and stdout-capture behavior. There is no test exercising a timeout, a stderr merge, a non-zero exit, or a long-running/hung command.

Mocks subprocess.Popen so the fake process reports returncode 1 and stdout.read yielding 'Error message' then None. It asserts Linter.run_cmd returns a result whose .text contains 'Error message', pinning the non-zero-exit error path. test_run_cmd (lines 30-38) is the complementary case with returncode 0, asserting the method returns None (zero exit = clean). test_run_cmd_with_special_chars (lines 61-80) verifies that a path with special characters ('src/(main)/product/[id]/page.tsx') survives shell quoting because it appears in the Popen command string. None of these tests configure or assert any timeout.

claims.claim: Neither aider/linter.py nor aider/run_cmd.py implements any timeout: run_cmd_subprocess passes no timeout to subprocess.Popen and blocks in a read(1) loop until EOF, run_cmd_pexpect calls interact() with no timeout until the child exits, and flake8_lint passes no timeout to subprocess.run. A hanging lint or shell command therefore blocks indefinitely.

Output capture merges stderr into stdout: run_cmd_subprocess sets stderr=subprocess.STDOUT on Popen and accumulates every decoded chunk (also echoing it in real time) into the string returned alongside the exit code; run_cmd_pexpect accumulates the same combined stream via an output_filter into a BytesIO decoded with errors="replace"; flake8_lint explicitly concatenates result.stdout + result.stderr.

Exit-status handling is: run_cmd_subprocess returns process.returncode from process.wait(); run_cmd_pexpect returns child.exitstatus (which may be None on signal); both, plus the run_cmd dispatcher, convert OSError/pexpect exceptions into exit status 1 with the error text as the output. Linter.run_cmd treats returncode == 0 as success (returns None) and only formats a failure when the status is non-zero, whereas flake8_lint ignores the exit status entirely and keys off non-empty captured text.

The tests exercise exit-status and output-capture semantics but contain no timeout coverage: test_run_cmd_echo asserts exit_code == 0 and exact captured stdout for a real echo; TestLinter.test_run_cmd and test_run_cmd_with_errors mock subprocess.Popen with returncode 0 and 1 respectively to assert None vs. an error-text result; test_run_cmd_with_special_chars asserts shell quoting of a special-character path. No test constructs a hanging command or asserts timeout behavior.

conclusion: aider's lint/command execution stack has no timeout mechanism at any layer. aider/run_cmd.py.run_cmd dispatches to run_cmd_pexpect when stdin is a TTY (interactive pass-through via interact(), returning child.exitstatus) or to run_cmd_subprocess otherwise. run_cmd_subprocess spawns with shell=True, stdout=PIPE, stderr=STDOUT (merging streams), decodes with errors="replace", echoes output byte-by-byte while accumulating it, then wait()s and returns (process.returncode, output); Popen receives no timeout, so hangs are unbounded. Exceptions in both branches are converted to exit status 1 with the error string as output. aider/linter.py consumes this: Linter.run_cmd quotes the filename, calls run_cmd_subprocess, and uses only stdout as lint text; a zero exit code means 'clean' (returns None) while a non-zero code is formatted as a '## Running: ...' block and parsed for file:line positions by errors_to_lint_result. Linter.flake8_lint is an independent path using subprocess.run(capture_output=True), concatenating stdout+stderr and deliberately ignoring the return code (check=False), relying instead on whether any output was produced. The tests confirm the exit-status/output-capture contract (echo returns 0 with exact stdout; mocked Popen returncode 0 vs 1 maps to None vs error result) but provide no timeout coverage, matching the absence of any timeout in the implementation.

These optional runtime dependencies are not installed and, per task constraints, dependencies were not installed. As a dependency-free fallback, `python -m py_compile aider/linter.py aider/run_cmd.py tests/basic/test_linter.py tests/basic/test_run_cmd.py` completed successfully (PY_COMPILE_OK), confirming all four files are syntactically valid.
